summary: Luke Badiali looked at client retention with Paul and Rebecca. Most engagements end after one savings wave and the relationship goes cold. We agreed a post-project savings tracking service and key account plans for the largest clients.

discussion.keyPoints: Rebecca's list showed 38 clients in three years but only 9 bought a second project.
Paul said clients often lose 20% to 30% of agreed savings within a year because contracts are not policed.
Gain-share contracts end after 12 months; there is no renewal conversation built in.

recommendations.recommendation: Offer a savings assurance retainer at £3,500 a month to track compliance after each project.
Name a client director for each of the top 6 clients with a quarterly business review.
Start the renewal conversation at month 9 of every 12-month gain-share contract.
Invite satisfied CFOs to speak at the CFO breakfasts.

actions.action: Write the savings assurance retainer offer

nextFocus: Model fees, margins and unit economics across gain-share and fixed fee.
nextPreparation: Paul to bring margin by engagement and gain-share cash receipts for the last two years.

tests.question: What retainer did we agree to offer after projects?
Is the month 9 renewal conversation agreed?
What did we agree for our top clients?
